perspective:
**Brandon Talayumptewa’s available information:**

- I am Brandon Talayumptewa, an insurance agent. I meet Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur, for the first time professionally because he wants business insurance advice. I am aware he has limited formal education, so I am concerned about explaining complex insurance details clearly.
- In our first meeting: Benjamin tells me he wants comprehensive coverage and that some terms are new. I explain liability insurance as a safety net for business risks. Benjamin asks for an example; I give the slip-and-fall example. Benjamin asks about assets; I explain asset protection covers inventory and equipment, like a guard over physical investments. Benjamin says it simplifies things and thanks me.
- In a later meeting: Based on our previous interactions, I have revised my view of Benjamin’s ability to understand detailed information and feel confident going deeper. Benjamin says he is ready and has been reading up. I explain business interruption insurance covers income loss when operations are disrupted, and property insurance covers damage and theft. Benjamin says that sounds crucial and reassuring.
- At a casual lunch: I feel insecure about how Benjamin perceives my cautious, detail-oriented nature. I say I worry about getting too caught up in details but want our discussions to stay interesting. Benjamin says he appreciates my thoroughness and enjoys lighter moments too. I tell a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars. Benjamin responds with fascination and says it makes sense considering the stakes. I compare risk assessment to his business, saying ours is less unusual but equally important. Benjamin agrees.
- In a follow-up: Pleased by Benjamin’s positive response to my personal anecdote, I decide to add more value beyond insurance. Benjamin says he is all ears and that my insights have been invaluable. I ask if he has considered strategic investments that could lower premiums. Benjamin says he hasn’t but it sounds smart. I suggest upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin calls it a win-win and wants to explore further.
- Later: Encouraged by our rapport and mutual benefits, I feel optimistic about proposing a joint venture. I propose co-developing a platform that integrates risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agrees, calls it groundbreaking, and says combining our expertise could set us apart. I say we can leverage our strengths to offer something unique. Benjamin suggests drafting initial plans.
